intervention_dose: 13.5 mg PO once daily, 2 weeks on / 1 week off (21-day cycle)
indication: Previously treated advanced/metastatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement
population_detail: FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement cohort (cohort A), prior gemcitabine-based chemotherapy; ECOG 0-2
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AE in 64% of the safety population (N=146). Hyperphosphatemia is the on-target class effect (55% any grade, no grade 3-4); hypophosphatemia reached grade 3 in 12%. Ocular monitoring warranted for serous retinal detachment (4%).

toxicities.notes: grade 3 or worse, all-cause in safety population
on-target FGFR class effect; no grade 3-4

notes: Pivotal trial driving FDA accelerated approval of pemigatinib in FGFR2-fusion CCA. Gated on a confirmed FGFR2 fusion, untested here (ngs_pending); efficacy and safety pulled from PMC full text PMC8461541.

indication: Previously treated advanced intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement
population_detail: Centrally confirmed FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement in intrahepatic CCA, >=1 prior line; activity retained against some pemigatinib-resistance kinase-domain mutations
safety_summary: Treatment-related grade 3+ AEs led by hyperphosphatemia (30%), the on-target class effect. Only 2% discontinued for treatment-related AEs and there were no treatment-related deaths; quality of life held steady on treatment.

toxicities.notes: on-target FGFR class effect; most common grade 3 TRAE

notes: Irreversible FGFR1-4 inhibitor with activity against some acquired FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance mutations, relevant for sequencing after pemigatinib. Efficacy from NEJM full text; toxicities are the grade 3+ rates reported in the abstract/results, full per-term table not extracted.

indication: Previously treated advanced cholangiocarcinoma with IDH1 R132 mutation
population_detail: IDH1 R132-mutant CCA after 1-2 prior regimens; crossover from placebo to ivosidenib permitted on progression
safety_summary: Grade 3+ AE profile similar to placebo; ascites was the most common grade 3+ event in both arms (7%). No treatment-related deaths. OS benefit blunted in the intention-to-treat analysis by 70% placebo-to-ivosidenib crossover, with the crossover-adjusted HR 0.46.
notes: Randomized phase 3 supporting FDA approval of ivosidenib in IDH1-mutant CCA. Gated on a confirmed IDH1 R132 mutation, untested here. Full efficacy/safety from PMC full text PMC7523268.

indication: Previously treated HER2-amplified biliary tract cancer
population_detail: Cohort 1: HER2 amplified by ISH plus IHC 2+/3+ (4B5 companion antibody); prior gemcitabine-based therapy

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 33 confirmed responders; cohort 1, independent central review

safety_summary: Most common grade 3 treatment-related events were diarrhea (5%) and decreased ejection fraction (3%); infusion-related reactions occurred in 35% (any grade) and diarrhea in 40%. Cardiac monitoring warranted given the ejection-fraction signal.
notes: Pivotal trial driving FDA accelerated approval of zanidatamab in HER2-positive (IHC 3+) BTC. Gating test is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH, not NGS alone, and is untested here. Efficacy/safety from Lancet Oncology abstract and conference follow-up.

indication: HER2-expressing biliary tract cancer (pan-tumor basket cohort)
population_detail: Biliary tract cohort of a HER2-expressing solid-tumor basket; central HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+. IHC 3+ subgroup responded markedly better than the overall cohort

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.subgroup: biliary tract cohort, all HER2 levels

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: IHC 3+ responders across study; mDoR 22.1 mo in IHC 3+

safety_summary: Grade 3+ drug-related AEs in 40.8% across the study; adjudicated drug-related interstitial lung disease in 10.5%, with three treatment-related deaths attributed to ILD. ILD risk should weigh in the decision although no toxicity veto was set in preferences.

toxicities.notes: adjudicated drug-related; characteristic T-DXd class effect
common GI TRAE; per-term rate not separated for biliary cohort

notes: Biomarker-defined pan-tumor basket; biliary patients enroll via a HER2-expressing cohort, so the IHC score drives expected benefit. ILD is the defining safety concern. AE rates are study-wide, not biliary-cohort-specific, per the JCO report.

intervention_dose: Dabrafenib 150 mg PO BID + trametinib 2 mg PO once daily
population_detail: Molecularly confirmed BRAF V600E (NGS/PCR; VE1 IHC suggestive but not sufficient); non-V600E class 2/3 BRAF alterations do not qualify
design: Open-label, single-arm phase 2 basket, biliary cohort (ROAR)
safety_summary: Serious AEs in 40%, treatment-related in 21% (mostly pyrexia, 19%). Most frequent grade 3+ event was increased gamma-glutamyltransferase (12%). No treatment-related deaths. Pyrexia is the characteristic combination class effect.
notes: ROAR biliary cohort plus the tumor-agnostic BRAF V600E label give two routes to treatment. Gated on a molecularly confirmed BRAF V600E, untested here. Durability/OS from conference and OncLive follow-up.

indication: MSI-H/dMMR advanced noncolorectal solid tumors (incl. biliary)
population_detail: MSI-H/dMMR by PCR or IHC; 27 tumor types, cholangiocarcinoma among the most common. No CCA-specific subgroup ORR published
safety_summary: Treatment-related grade 3-5 AEs in 14.6%; one grade 5 pneumonia, no other treatment-related deaths. Immune-mediated AEs are the characteristic checkpoint-inhibitor concern.
notes: Tumor-agnostic basket admitting MSI-H/dMMR biliary cancer on the biomarker; MSI-H is rare in BTC (~1-3%) but decision-changing. No CCA-specific subgroup ORR reported in this publication.

indication: TMB-high advanced solid tumors (>=10 mut/Mb), incl. biliary
population_detail: tTMB-high >=10 mut/Mb on FoundationOne CDx; biliary admitted through the biomarker, not a dedicated cohort
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR not reached (range 2.2+ to 34.8+); mPFS 2.1 mo; mOS 11.7 mo

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 30/102; abstract reports 28.3% (95% CI 20.5-37.3) in full population analysis

safety_summary: Safety mirrors the broader KEYNOTE-158 pembrolizumab population; this biomarker analysis did not report separate grade 3+ rates for the TMB-high subgroup.
notes: TMB-high subgroup analysis supporting the tumor-agnostic TMB-high label; the same CGP that resolves the other axes returns this value. Toxicities[] empty because this biomarker-analysis publication reports no per-term safety for the subgroup (abstract and ASCO Post summary checked; safety deferred to the parent KEYNOTE-158 reports).

indication: NTRK fusion-positive advanced solid tumors (integrated basket)
population_detail: NTRK1/2/3 fusion across tumor types; biliary patients enroll on the fusion regardless of subsite
design: Integrated analysis of three phase 1-2 trials (ALKA-372-001, STARTRK-1, STARTRK-2)
safety_summary: In the updated NTRK safety population (n=193), grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs in 41.5%, led by weight gain (8.3%), anemia (5.2%), and fatigue (4.7%). Characteristic any-grade AEs include dysgeusia (35%) and dizziness, reflecting CNS-penetrant TRK inhibition.
notes: Tumor-agnostic NTRK-fusion basket; rare in CCA (<1%), best caught by RNA-based fusion NGS. Efficacy from the 2020 Lancet Oncology paper; safety rates from the 2022 updated integrated analysis (PMC9365368) since the original per-term grade 3-4 table was not separately accessible.

indication: TRK fusion-positive advanced solid tumors (pooled basket)
population_detail: NTRK1/2/3 fusion across tumor types and ages; biliary patients treated on the fusion irrespective of subsite
design: Pooled analysis of three phase 1/2 trials (incl. NAVIGATE)
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR 35.2 mo; mPFS 28.3 mo; mOS 44.4 mo
safety_summary: Across the 260-patient safety population, grade 3 AEs in 13% and grade 4 in <1%; most common grade 3+ events were increased ALT (3%), anemia (2%), and decreased neutrophils (2%). No treatment-related deaths.
notes: Highly selective TRK inhibitor with a tumor-agnostic label and the most durable responses among the fusion inhibitors. Same rare-fusion gate as entrectinib. Safety from the 260-patient pooled safety population.

indication: RET fusion-positive solid tumors other than lung/thyroid (basket)
population_detail: RET fusion-positive non-lung/non-thyroid tumors; 58% had refractory GI malignancies. Biliary patients enroll on a confirmed RET fusion
safety_summary: Among all 45 patients, grade 3+ AEs in 56%, led by hypertension (22%), increased ALT (16%), and increased AST (13%). Three grade 5 treatment-emergent events (7%). Hypertension and transaminase elevation are the characteristic class effects.
notes: Tumor-agnostic RET-fusion basket covering non-lung/non-thyroid tumors; RET fusions are rare in CCA and need RNA-based fusion NGS. ORR is on 41 evaluable of 45 enrolled.

indication: KRAS G12C-mutated advanced solid tumors, biliary tract cancer cohort
population_detail: KRAS G12C-mutant pretreated GI tumors; biliary tract cancer cohort n=12 within a pan-tumor basket
median_dor_or_pfs: Pan-cohort mDoR 5.3 mo; mPFS 8.6 mo; mOS 15.1 mo

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 5/12 responders; 95% CI not separately reported for the small biliary cohort

safety_summary: Grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs in 27% of the treated population (n=63); most common any-grade TRAEs were nausea (49%), diarrhea (48%), fatigue (41%), and vomiting (40%). GI toxicity is the characteristic class effect.
notes: Published KRYSTAL-1 biliary cohort (n=12) gives a small but on-indication KRAS G12C readout, supersedes the no-readout basket NCT05722327 on trials.jsonl. KRAS G12C is rare in CCA (~1%) and gated on tumor NGS.

exclusion_reason: Phase 1 dose-escalation (NCT06160752) with no published efficacy or safety readout yet. Next-generation FGFR2 inhibitor relevant if the patient is FGFR2-positive and progresses on pemigatinib/futibatinib, but there is no clinical-evidence paper to compile.
Ongoing first-line phase 3 (NCT06467357) with no readout. The T-DXd evidence base is already captured from DESTINY-PanTumor02; this row would add a registration-only entry with no published outcomes.
Ongoing first-line phase 3 (NCT06282575) with no readout. The zanidatamab evidence base is captured from HERIZON-BTC-01; nothing published to extract here.
Registry-only basket entry with no standalone readout; superseded by the published KRYSTAL-1 biliary cohort (PMID 37099736), which is compiled as an included row.

intervention_dose: 12 mg PO once daily (recommended phase 2 dose)
indication: Advanced solid tumors, cholangiocarcinoma subset with FGFR2 alterations
population_detail: Dose-escalation/expansion; 14/48 had cholangiocarcinoma, 11 evaluable, all with disease control carried FGFR2 alterations including post-FGFR-inhibitor resistance
design: First-in-human, open-label phase 1 dose escalation/expansion (single agent)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 3/11 PR; a 4th had SD >=24 weeks (clinical benefit 36.4%)

safety_summary: Grade 3+ events in 43.8% with no grade 4-5; hypertension was the dominant on-target multikinase effect (50% any grade, 27.1% grade 3). PPE, stomatitis, diarrhea, and nausea were mostly low-grade.
notes: Phase 1 that seeded the tinengotinib phase 3 (NCT07328919) in FGFR2-altered CCA; the disease-control signal concentrated in FGFR2-altered patients, including some who had progressed on a prior FGFR inhibitor. Gated on an untested FGFR2 alteration. AE and subset data from the Oncologist full text.

intervention_dose: 70 mg PO once daily (recommended phase 2 dose)
indication: FGFR-inhibitor-naive, chemotherapy-pretreated cholangiocarcinoma with FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement
population_detail: FGFRi-naive CCA harboring FGFR2 fusions/rearrangements after prior chemotherapy; pivotal ReFocus cohort
journal: Journal of Clinical Oncology (ASCO GI 2026 abstract 476)
safety_summary: The FGFR2-selective design largely spares FGFR1-driven hyperphosphatemia; the leading grade 3+ treatment-related events were palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia (32.8%) and stomatitis (12.1%).
notes: FGFR2-selective inhibitor; the ReFocus CCA cohort supports an NDA under FDA priority review (PDUFA Sept 2026). Abstract-only; no PubMed record, so pmid is null. AE detail beyond the two headline grade 3+ terms not in the abstract.

safety_summary: Grade 3+ treatment-emergent AEs in 35.3%, led by transaminase elevation, nail disorders, and anemia. One serious treatment-related event, no treatment-related deaths, and no AE-driven discontinuations.

safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicities. Any-grade TEAEs above 15%: nausea 43%, fatigue 25%, decreased appetite 22%, AST increase 18%, ALT increase 16%, constipation 16%. Grade-resolved rates not given in the abstract.

The IHCC subset (n=26) response numbers sat in an abstract table (see-text) not reproduced in the retrievable text, so effect_size is null.
